questions.q: What is the purpose of 'cutting off transaction entry' at the start of a month-end close?
options: To permanently delete the period's transactions
To begin the next fiscal year early
To stop new postings to the period being closed, so its numbers hold still while being reviewed
To automatically generate the balance sheet
questions.explain: Cutoff stops new postings to the closing period so its figures remain stable while the close checklist proceeds.

questions.q: In what order do these typically occur in a month-end close?
options: Financial statements are generated before the trial balance is reviewed
The period is closed before any adjusting entries are recorded
Reversing entries are posted before the transaction cutoff
Adjusting entries and the trial balance review happen before financial statements are generated
questions.explain: The checklist proceeds: cutoff, subledger close, adjusting entries, reconciliation, trial balance review, then financial statements, review, and period close.

questions.q: What happens to revenue and expense accounts specifically at year-end that does NOT happen at a routine month-end close?
options: They are permanently deleted from the chart of accounts
They are closed (zeroed out), with their net effect rolled into Retained Earnings
They are converted into liabilities
Nothing different happens to them at year-end
questions.explain: At year-end, temporary accounts (revenue and expenses) are closed into Retained Earnings so the next fiscal year starts with a fresh income statement.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what does a slow, error-prone close usually indicate?
options: That something upstream in the accounting cycle needs attention — miscoded transactions, subledgers not reconciling, or manual processes that should be automated
That the company is highly profitable
That the fiscal calendar needs to be changed
Nothing useful — close speed has no diagnostic value
questions.explain: Close speed and accuracy are a visible signal of how well the upstream accounting cycle (transactions, subledgers, reconciliations) is functioning.
